messages:
Priya: Heads up — I ran a focused profiling pass on continuous batching for the payments route. P95 is drifting above our 180ms target during peak qps. Observed a couple of suspicious patterns: kernel switch churn + KV cache evictions when bursts align.
Kevin: Can you paste the perf traces and the config you used?
Priya: Sure — short dump below (trimmed):
```
trace: batch_form_time=12ms, exec_start=0.8ms, kernel_switches=3, kv_cache_evictions=42
route=payments, tier=premium, p95=238ms, p50=72ms, qps=420
microbatch_size=8, token_budget_target=120
```
Priya: Notable: kernel_switches spiked when seq_len variance > 0.4 and when the queue policy allowed large older requests to sit behind many small ones. That forces microbatch reassembly and extra kernel launches.
Marta: That aligns with yesterday's kernel-selector PR — it trades launching fewer huge kernels for more optimal per-batch kernels. Good for throughput but may hurt p95 for small-latency routes.
Kevin: So two knobs: (1) queue policy (age-vs-size) and (2) dynamic token_budget per route/tier. We can prefer smaller requests for latency-sensitive routes.
Jon: Quick experiment idea: set token_budget_target lower for payments premium (e.g., 80) and bias queue to prefer reqs with seq_len <= 128 for that route. See if p95 drops without hurting overall throughput.
Priya: I ran that locally — results looked promising: p95 fell from 238ms -> 165ms, p50 unchanged. CPU kernel switch rate down 48%. KV evictions also down ~30%.
perf-bot: Canary run results (us-west-2): 24h window: payments-premium p95=170ms (-28%), overall throughput -2%, error rate unchanged. Metrics: avg_kernel_launches_per_min -40%.
SRE oncall: Important to verify tail behavior under multi-tenant noise. Also watch memory pressure; lower token budgets may increase batching frequency.
Marta: Agreed. Also need to ensure we don't regress other routes. Suggest: add per-route policy config, with these defaults:
```
queue_policy:
  payments:
    tier_overrides:
      premium: { token_budget: 80, prefer_short: true }
      standard: { token_budget: 120, prefer_short: false }
  default:
    token_budget: 100
    prefer_short: false
```
Priya: I'll open a perf ticket and a small PR that wires this into the router. Test plan: 1) Unit + synthetic load 2) Canary in us-west-2 with 10% traffic 3) Gradual ramp to 50% if p95 < 185ms and error rate stable.
Kevin: Also add a metric export: token_budget_effective_by_route and kernel_switch_count_by_route so we can correlate quickly.
Jon: One more gotcha — KV cache key churn. If we bias for short requests, we might reduce reuse for long chat sessions. We should exempt routes tagged `kv_hot` (e.g., chat-sessions) from prefer_short.
Priya: Good call. I'll add a route label check.
Marta: If canary looks good, we should roll this into the next minor runtime release. Document the risk: slight throughput dip for aggregated system but big p95 wins for latency-sensitive customers.
SRE oncall: I'll schedule the canary and attach the rollback playbook.
Priya: Opening PR/issue now: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/8234 (WIP) — will post updates and the final perf dashboard link once Canary finishes. :rocket:
Kevin: Thanks — nice triage + actionable plan. :+1:
Priya: Thanks team. I'll follow up with the full traces and a short runbook for oncall if we need to revert.
